chapterTitle: Stock Index Options, Currency Options, Portfolio Insurance, and Dividend Adjustments

beatOutlines.textOutline: A portfolio manager asks how index options like S&P 500 (SPX) settle since you cannot physically deliver an entire stock index ([fact-01]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The mentor explains cash settlement: exercise triggers a cash payment based on the difference between strike and index settlement value (SET) ([fact-01]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Each standard index option contract incorporates a $100 multiplier, scaling cash flows for institutional and retail portfolios ([fact-01]).

scenes.title: Stock Pricing vs. Continuous Dividend Yield Adjustment

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Zero-Dividend Stock: underlying stock price is simply S0 in standard BSM formulas ([fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Continuous Dividend Yield q: S0 is replaced by prepaid forward price S0 * e^(-q*T) in generalized BSM formulas and put-call parity c + K*e^(-r*T) = p + S0*e^(-q*T) ([fact-02], [fact-03], [fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Floor Protection: purchasing index put options establishes an absolute minimum portfolio floor while preserving upside ([fact-06]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Beta Sizing Formula: N = beta * (P / (100 * I)), requiring 50% more contracts when portfolio beta equals 1.5 ([fact-07]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine Popular Claim: belief that stocks are guaranteed to outperform bonds over long horizons like 20-30 years due to expected drift ([fact-10]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine Put Option Reality: Hull proves put protection cost does NOT vanish as T increases because volatility uncertainty sigma * sqrt(T) continues growing ([fact-10]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Gross Protection Payoff vs. Compounded Net Return

beatOutlines.textOutline: Balance Gross Payoff: terminal protection equals max(K - S_T, 0), providing nominal downside cash recovery ([fact-11]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Balance Net Trading Profit: strictly defined as payoff minus initial premium compounded at risk-free rate (Payoff - Premium paid * e^(r*T)), avoiding fatal budgeting errors ([fact-11]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot Foreign Currency Yield: foreign interest rate rf acts as continuous dividend yield q in BSM pricing formulas ([fact-08]).

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot GBP Call Pricing Profile: spot 1.60, domestic rate 6%, foreign rate 8%, yielding $0.0431 per GBP option value ([fact-09]).

beatOutlines.textOutline: Generalized Put-Call Parity: c + K*e^(-r*T) = p + S0*e^(-q*T) enforcing synthetic arbitrage bounds for dividend-paying assets ([fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Garman-Kohlhagen Parity: replacing q with rf adapts parity directly for foreign exchange spot and option markets ([fact-08]).

summarySteps: 1. Index Option Cash Settlement ([fact-01]): Index options feature $100 multipliers and settle in cash against index settlement value (SET).
2. Prepaid Forward Pricing ([fact-02]): Continuous dividend yields q reduce effective stock price from S0 to S0 * e^(-q*T) in all valuation formulas.
3. Generalized BSM Formulas ([fact-03]): Incorporate continuous dividend yields into cumulative normal probabilities N(d1) and N(d2).
4. Dividend Put-Call Parity ([fact-04]): c + K*e^(-r*T) = p + S0*e^(-q*T) establishes synthetic arbitrage bounds.
5. Portfolio Insurance Sizing ([fact-07]): Beta-adjusted hedge contracts require N = beta * (P / (100 * I)) to neutralize systematic market risk.
6. Garman-Kohlhagen Model ([fact-08]): Foreign currency options substitute foreign risk-free rate rf for continuous dividend yield q.
7. Long-Term Guarantees ([fact-10]): Long-term underperformance insurance remains costly because volatility uncertainty sigma * sqrt(T) continues growing.
8. Net Trading Profit ([fact-11]): True net profit requires compounding initial put premiums at the risk-free rate: Profit = Payoff - Premium paid * e^(r*T).
bottomTakeaway: Stock index and currency options generalize the Black-Scholes-Merton model through prepaid forward price adjustments and foreign risk-free rates, enabling precise beta-adjusted portfolio insurance and cash-settled risk management ([fact-01], [fact-03], [fact-07], [fact-08]).
